\chapter{Sorting-Based Greedy}
\label{ch:sorting_greedy}

\begin{tcolorbox}[enhanced, colback=white, colframe=secondaryblue, boxrule=1pt, arc=2mm]
\textbf{\large\textcolor{primaryblue}{Most greedies start with a sort: by value, by deadline, by a difference or by a ratio --- the key is the whole algorithm.}}
\end{tcolorbox}

\textbf{Part A --- Lessons}
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*, label=\textbf{A\arabic*.}, itemsep=1pt]
    \item Sorting by one key and processing in order
    \item Sorting by a difference $a_i - b_i$ or a ratio $a_i / b_i$
    \item Pairing after sorting: smallest with smallest, smallest with largest
    \item Sorting both sides of an assignment
    \item Ties and stability: when the order of equal keys matters
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*, label=\textbf{P\arabic*.}, itemsep=1pt]
    \item \textbf{Sort by one key} --- Advantage Shuffle {\small\color{darkgray}(LeetCode 870)}, Minimum Number of Moves to Seat Everyone {\small\color{darkgray}(LeetCode 2037)}
    \item \textbf{Sort by a difference or position} --- Two City Scheduling {\small\color{darkgray}(LeetCode 1029)}, Maximum Number of Coins You Can Get {\small\color{darkgray}(LeetCode 1561)}
